problem: The last sentence says the load currents' phasor sum is 'no longer forced through the neutral', which reads as if the sum is now non-zero. With the neutral open there is no return path, so by KCL at the load star point the three load currents must sum to exactly zero; that is precisely why the star point shifts.
fix: The neutral current in the opened wire is zero. Because no current can return, the three load currents must now sum to zero at the load star point; the star point shifts to a new voltage VN′N, which makes the three load phase voltages unequal and unequal currents whose phasor sum is zero.

problem: The note 'equal Z, 120° apart' puts the 120° spacing on the impedances. Impedances have no phase spacing; it is the three phase currents (or voltages) that are 120° apart.
fix: Note: 'equal Z per phase; currents 120° apart'.
